description: INTERMAGNET is the global network of cooperating digital magnetic observatories that monitor the Earth's magnetic field, set up from 1986 to 1987 as a pilot between the United States and British Geological Surveys and since expanded worldwide. Its programme adopts common standards for instruments and recording so that observatory data can be exchanged and geomagnetic products produced in close to real time, and it helps new observatories get established. The site provides data download and plots, format specifications and quality checking rules for preliminary and definitive observatory time series of the magnetic field components, with definitive data published annually. Unless otherwise noted the data are licensed CC BY-NC 4.0: free for non-commercial use, while commercial use, sale or bulk redistribution needs written permission of the operating institute, and some institutes set different conditions listed on the data conditions page. DOIs exist for part of the data only. Caveats: station coverage is uneven, oceans and parts of Africa and Asia are sparse, and preliminary data contain artefacts. It is the observational basis for geomagnetically induced current studies of power grids and pipelines, for hazard exposure and resilience analysis of space weather, and for model validation; related records are the GFZ Kp index and NOAA SWPC products.
